name: attalla1/photopea-mcp-server
methodology_note: Repo-surface track: this product is distributed as a repository (MCP server) with no web product surface, so the score derives ONLY from measurable public-repository signals — documentation, licensing, maintenance activity, releases, traction, agent-consumability. Each checklist item carries its evidence. Score ceiling 82/100: VITAL requires hands-on behavioral testing that repo signals cannot provide. Replaces a 2026-06/07 stub that carried a default score with no evidence.

checklist.task: Maintained: pushed within 12 months and not archived
Agent-consumable surface documented (MCP config or CLI install)

summary: attalla1/photopea-mcp-server — MCP server for AI-driven image editing with Photopea. Repo-surface review: measured from the public repository (23 stars, MIT, last push 2026-04-05); not hands-on tested.

hlido_opinion.headline: A tidy MIT-licensed MCP server that hands agents Photopea's image-editing surface — genuinely agent-native, but early (23 stars) and quiet for ~5 months.
hlido_opinion.body: This is a focused, well-formed piece of agent plumbing: an MCP server that lets an AI agent design posters, edit photos and transform images by driving Photopea, the free browser-based Photoshop alternative. Because it speaks MCP, it is agent-consumable by construction — the checklist confirms it — and it ships MIT-licensed with documented install and tagged releases, which is more release discipline than most tools this size show. The cautions are about maturity and momentum, not design: it has only 23 stars, no CI, and its last push was in early April 2026 — roughly five months quiet — so confirm it still tracks Photopea before depending on it. It is also a thin bridge over a third-party service, so its usefulness is bounded by Photopea's continued availability. Repo-surface read; the editing quality itself was not tested hands-on.

tier_rationale: STEADY (80, repo-surface ceiling). MIT licensing, documented install, tagged releases and — crucially — genuine agent-consumability over MCP clear STEADY. VITAL is withheld because traction is low (23 stars), there is no CI, the repo has been quiet for ~5 months, and editing quality is unverified from the repo surface.
what_it_does_well: Genuinely agent-native — exposes image editing to agents over MCP
MIT-licensed with documented install and tagged releases
Clear, narrow scope: drives Photopea, a free browser-based Photoshop alternative
Gives agents an image-editing capability without a paid design API
what_it_fails_at: Low traction (23 stars) and no CI present
Last push ~5 months ago — momentum has cooled
A thin wrapper over third-party Photopea — bounded by that service's availability
Editing quality and reliability unverified hands-on
best_for: Agent builders who need an image-editing tool callable over MCP
Workflows wanting programmatic poster/photo edits without a paid design API
not_recommended_for: Teams needing an actively-maintained, high-traction dependency
Use cases that cannot tolerate reliance on a third-party (Photopea) surface
red_flags: Quiet for ~5 months with no CI — confirm it still tracks Photopea before depending on it

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: An MCP server an agent connects to directly to drive Photopea for image editing; agent-consumable by construction. Behaviorally testable via MCP but not run hands-on for this review.
